correctness.rationale: Every open set is saturated and the quotient is finite, so the least open neighborhood in C_q is the union of C_r for r≥q. A finite union meets A infinitely exactly when some contributing class meets it infinitely. This proves the operator formula even for uncountable fibers. Choosing entire infinite classes realizes every possible set J(A). For each ideal K of I the image F(K) is the union of classes in ↓_Q K; restriction to I recovers K, proving the order isomorphism, and applying the formula to such an image proves idempotence. For two ideals K,L their set intersection has infinite-class trace K∩L, so the only possible image equal to that intersection is F(K∩L). With a least infinite class i_q above q, C_q belongs to F(K) exactly when i_q∈K. If the nonempty upper trace has no least element, two distinct minimal members in the finite trace have no common lower bound there. Their two principal ideals produce C_q in the intersection but not in F(K∩L). The obstructing q must be finite and distinct from these two infinite classes, proving three-class sharpness. Birkhoff representation identifies I with the nonzero join-irreducible poset of the image order in every realization; countable infinite copies of those points attain the lower bound and force quotient-order uniqueness. The singleton case is separate. The symbolic verifier and its reported 3670 cases were inspected, not executed; they are not required for the proof.

evidence: Montacute proves finite underlying spaces have trivial ω-accumulation and proves Ω²(A)⊆Ω(A) generally. The transitive-frame realization concerns countable T0 spaces and restricted valuations; the prefix-tree and ordinal records concern branching/rank and chain normal forms, respectively.
Birkhoff identifies finite distributive lattices with ideals of their join-irreducibles.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A finite underlying space has I empty, unlike a finite quotient in general. The cited realization and infinite-host order classes do not yield the all-subset marked-fiber classification for arbitrary finite posets. Birkhoff supplies the inverse poset once the actual operator image is identified, but gives no ordinary-intersection criterion in the ambient power set.

value.rationale: For a standard topological modality, the result describes all outputs on a class allowing arbitrary cardinality and every subset, not just a finite test slice. The value is chiefly the sharp criterion separating the abstract meet from the actual set intersection, with a smallest obstruction, and the exact constraint on which quotient can realize a given image order minimally. Neither the elementary finite-union observation nor the textbook Birkhoff deduction alone would warrant the same assessment.
